title: BullBrief
summary: An equity research tool that reads market data, filings, and earnings, then writes the brief an analyst would have spent an afternoon on.
content: Equity research starts the same way every time: pull the filings, skim the earnings call, check the fundamentals, and write it up. BullBrief does the pulling and the first draft.

A Next.js frontend takes a ticker and returns a structured digest — business model, financial health, recent developments. Behind it, a Python service fans out to yFinance and SEC data, normalizes what comes back, and runs it through prompts tuned for financial language rather than general summarization.
The hard part was not the AI. It was making a page that stays fast and legible while it waits on four data sources that fail independently.
features: Ticker search with autocomplete and validation
Live market and fundamentals data via yFinance
Deep Compare mode for side-by-side company breakdowns
Financial-domain prompt design over a general summarizer
Rate-limit and partial-failure handling across data sources
lessons: Designing financial interfaces around speed and legibility
Prompting for a domain instead of prompting for a summary
Degrading gracefully when one of four upstream sources is down

title: UniVizr
summary: Degree planning that treats a transcript as a graph — what you have taken, what it unlocks, and which industry skills it maps to.
content: Course catalogs are graphs pretending to be lists. Prerequisites, corequisites, and substitutions form a dependency structure that no advising spreadsheet models well, which is why degree planning goes wrong.

UniVizr stores that structure properly in PostgreSQL and exposes it through a FastAPI service, so a student can see progress, generate a viable semester plan, and trace coursework to the skills it actually builds.
Built with a partner, which made API contracts and review discipline matter more than they do on a solo project.
features: Degree progress visualization with milestone tracking
Generated semester plans that respect prerequisite structure
Async FastAPI endpoints with request validation
Relational schema built for prerequisite graphs
lessons: Modeling prerequisite structure as a graph, not a checklist
Holding an API contract steady across two developers
Where generated plans need a human override

title: Athlytics
summary: NBA player analytics — advanced stats and awards history served from a cached Basketball-Reference pipeline.
content: A basketball research tool built to answer the arguments that come up constantly and get settled badly: who actually had the better peak, how a season stacks up historically, what the award voting really looked like.

The interesting engineering is the pipeline rather than the interface. Basketball-Reference is slow and unfriendly to repeated queries, so a Python backend scrapes, normalizes, and caches per-player records to disk, keyed by the site's own player IDs. The frontend then reads from cache and stays quick.
Archived at the point where the data layer worked and the interface had not caught up. Left up because the caching approach is the part worth showing.
features: Per-player award and advanced-stat records, cached to disk
Normalization layer over inconsistent upstream tables
Cache keyed by Basketball-Reference player IDs
lessons: Caching is the whole design when the upstream source is slow
Normalize at ingest, not at read time
Knowing when to archive a side project instead of finishing it
